name: Nepalese Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Sapkota, Sharada & Bhim Lal Gautam. 2025. Nepali Sign Language and Deaf Education Pedagogy in Nepal: Issues and Way Forwards. Nepalese Linguistics 39(1). doi:10.3126/nl.v39i1.86212
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Education/policy paper; nothing on phonology or stress ('stress' occurs only as psychological stress).

sources.citation: Gautam, Bhim Lal & Sharada Sapkota. 2024. Sociolinguistics of Nepali sign language: Orientation and movement. Journal of Nepalese Studies 16(1): 5-16. doi:10.3126/jns.v16i1.71775
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Journal condensation of Sapkota 2023: places of articulation, six palm / five knuckle orientations, path vs local movement, non-manuals. Silent on stress/prominence.

sources.citation: Sapkota, Sharada. 2023. Phonological Parameters in Nepali Sign Language. MA dissertation, Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu. 59 pp. (hdl:20.500.14540/20016)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing language-specific. The whole thesis is sign phonology in Brentari's (1998) Prosodic Model: ch.2 inherent features (handshape, place of articulation: head/arm/body/hand, six palm orientations), ch.3 'Prosodic features' = setting change, path (arc/circle/straight/trilled), orientation change, aperture change, 35 movement types, seven non-manual categories. 'Stress' appears only in a generic definition (p.34, repeated pp.41, 49-50): 'prosody in any language either speech or signing, refers to the study of rhythmic structure, intonation, stress.. sources.citation: Green, E. Mara. 2009. Nepali Sign Language and Nepali: Social and Linguistic Dimensions of a Case of Inter-Modal Language Contact. Proceedings of the Berkeley Linguistics Society 35(2). doi:10.3765/bls.v35i2.3508
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kinship-term contact study; only remarks that 'the phonological systems of NSL and Nepali are almost definitionally incompatible'. Nothing on stress.
